title: Stage 2 of a case: recap the client, the problem and the goal in one or two sentences
description: Shows you listened, and checks you are solving the right problem. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
hook: A recap is your chance to make sure you and the interviewer are solving the same problem. It takes fifteen seconds and saves you from the worst mistake in casing: answering the wrong question.
body:
Stage 2 of 10 in the ten stages of a case.

Why it matters

Shows you listened, and checks you are solving the right problem.

The common mistake

Reading the whole prompt back word for word.

What to do, and what to say

Recap the key points only

The client, the problem and the measurable goal. Then check.

"So our client is X, facing Y, and success means Z by [date]. Did I get that right?"

Practise the moment

Read the situation and say your answer out loud before you open the model.

The prompt was: a UK gym chain, revenue up 5%, profit halved, the CEO wants it fixed within a year. Give your recap.

Show a strong answer

"So our client is a UK gym chain whose revenue is growing but profit has halved, and success means restoring profit within a year. Did I get that right?"

Why it works: Client, problem, measurable goal, then a check. Three sentences at most.

Next stage: clarifying questions (three at most).
outro: Read it once, then try it on a practice case today while it is fresh. One real attempt teaches more than three re-reads. All ten stages, with every phrase, are on the free perfect casing page.
